note_on_method: Each venue page rests on three City of Irvine pages - the pickleball page that counts the courts, calls them lit and prices the reservable ones, the court regulations page that says how an open court is shared, and the park's own page that gives the address, the hours and the amenities - plus the US Census address geocoder for the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence; where the City and the Census disagree on a postcode, both values are stated.

slots.description:
Eight lit pickleball courts, the largest set in Irvine, in a community park of approximately 22 acres that the City lists under its Woodbridge facilities.

The count rests on two City records. The pickleball page reads "eight lit pickleball courts located at Mike Ward Community Park", and the park's own amenity list reads "8 Lighted Pickleball Courts". The regulations page repeats the eight under the shorter name Mike Ward Park. Nothing here is inferred from a map or a photograph; the City states the number three times and states the same number each time.

The rest of the amenity list describes the company the courts keep: two lighted basketball courts, three lighted racquetball courts, a sand volleyball court, a fitness parcourse, an amphitheatre, two drinking fountains, three restrooms, two barbecues, a picnic shelter and four picnic tables. Two of the eight courts, #3 and #4, are the reservable pair, which the City prices at $17 an hour for residents and $19 for non-residents. The other six are first come, first served, and the City states no price for them.
slots.getting_there:
20 Lake Road, Irvine, CA 92604. The US Census address geocoder matched the address at house-number level as "20 LAKE RD, IRVINE, CA, 92604", placed it in Orange County, and placed it in the incorporated place Irvine city, which is what lets it publish under Irvine. The City's own page prints the same postcode, so there is no disagreement to record here. The park's published phone number is 949-724-6900.

The City publishes nothing about parking at this park - no lot, no fee, no permit. There are three restrooms and two drinking fountains, both stated in the amenity list. Hours are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., daily.
slots.what_to_expect:
Eight lit courts, open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, running under two sets of rules at once.

Six of them are open courts, and the City's regulations govern them: "Open courts are on a first-come, first-serve basis. Please use the waiting board where available." When others are waiting, doubles has 60 minutes and singles 30, warm-up included, and groups may not camp on a court. Eight courts is enough for a rotation, and the waiting board is the City's own mechanism for running one.

Courts #3 and #4 can be booked online between 7 a.m. and noon and 4 and 10 p.m., in one- or two-hour blocks, one reservation per person per day; residents book five days ahead, non-residents three. When nobody has booked them they "can be used for drop-in play", and a drop-in player must "immediately vacate the court if a reservation holder arrives". The City also runs junior, adult and private lessons here through contract instructors, and its programmes take priority over all other use.

The City states no surface, no peak times and nothing about parking, and never calls these courts indoor or outdoor.

slots.description:
Six lit pickleball courts in a community park of approximately 32 acres in the north-east of the city, beside three lighted tennis courts, two lighted softball fields and two lighted soccer fields.

The count is stated twice by the City: "six lit pickleball courts located at Portola Springs Community Park" on its pickleball page, and "6 Lighted Pickleball Courts" in the park's own amenity list. The regulations page gives the same six. Courts #5 and #6 are the reservable pair, at $17 an hour for residents and $19 for non-residents; the other four are first come, first served.

This is also the home of Irvine Team Pickleball, the City's league, which the pickleball page places at these courts. The park has a community centre with a Native American Wing, which the City describes as a monument to its partnership with the Acjachemen people, whose village stood here, and the site includes 124 acres of preserved open space, trails and a native garden. The amenity list adds a concession building, a nature-themed playground, three picnic shelters, fifteen picnic tables and two restrooms.

slots.description:
Four lit pickleball courts in the largest of Irvine's three published parks, approximately 36.5 acres, with twelve lighted tennis courts alongside.

The City states the count twice: "four lit pickleball courts located at Heritage Park" on its pickleball page, and "4 Lighted Pickleball Courts" in the park's own amenity list. The regulations page, which repeats the counts for Mike Ward, Portola Springs and Los Olivos, leaves Heritage out of its list of lit pickleball courts altogether; the two records that do state a number agree, and four is published. The record this site imported before reading the City said two, which is why the venue is flagged for a re-read on the next cycle.

Heritage is also one of the parks the City names for its hybrid tennis-and-pickleball courts. Those are not added here, because the City gives only a city-wide figure for them - ten on one page, nine on another - and never says how many are at Heritage. The park has a community centre, a lake, a splash pad, an amphitheatre, three lighted soccer fields, three lighted basketball courts, two lighted ball diamonds and four restrooms, and the City is developing a master plan for it.
slots.getting_there:
14301 Yale Ave., Irvine, CA 92604, as the park's own page prints it. The US Census address geocoder matched "14301 YALE AVE, IRVINE, CA, 92604" at house-number level, in Orange County, in the incorporated place Irvine city. The City's postcode and the Census postcode agree. The park's published phone number is 949-724-6750.

The City publishes nothing about parking here, which is a more noticeable silence at a 36.5-acre park with twelve lighted tennis courts, three soccer fields and two ball diamonds than at a smaller site. There are four restrooms and eight drinking fountains in the amenity list. Hours are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., daily.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four lit courts, all of them open courts, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Nothing at Heritage can be reserved: the City's online booking covers Courts #3 and #4 at Mike Ward and Courts #5 and #6 at Portola Springs and no court here, so this is the one published Irvine venue where turning up is the only way in.

Four courts is two games at once rather than a rotation, and the City's regulations are what manage the queue: first come, first served, the waiting board where available, doubles limited to 60 minutes and singles to 30 when others are waiting, and no camping on a court by a group.

The twelve lighted tennis courts next door matter too. The City names Heritage among the parks with hybrid courts "where players may choose to play tennis or pickleball", and on tennis courts the rule is explicit: "Tennis courts are designated solely for tennis use", pickleball may use them only when no tennis player is waiting, and must vacate when tennis players arrive. The four dedicated courts carry no such condition. Lessons are taught here by the City's contract instructors. No surface, parking or peak times are stated.

faqs.a: Four dedicated pickleball courts, stated twice: "four lit pickleball courts located at Heritage Park" and "4 Lighted Pickleball Courts". The City's hybrid courts here are not counted, because it never says how many there are.
Yes, in the City's own word on both records, and the park is open until 10 p.m. daily.
No. The City's online booking covers two courts at Mike Ward and two at Portola Springs only. Every court at Heritage is first come, first served.
Not stated. The City calls these courts first come, first served and publishes no price for them, but it does not write the word free, so neither do we.
Yes, four, listed among the park's amenities on its own page, along with eight drinking fountains and a splash pad.
